material3_expressive.decision: androidx.compose.material3:material3 1.5.0-alpha28 (material3-android, minCompileSdk=37, minAGP=9.1.0). Compose stack aligned with BOM 2026.09.00 (ui/foundation 1.12.1 runtime — alpha28 declares 1.13.0-alpha01 api deps but is compatible against the 1.12.1 BOM train for the APIs used).
material3_expressive.why: Verification against the actual artifacts showed the Expressive public API surface is NOT in the 1.4.0 stable: in material3 1.4.0 MaterialExpressiveTheme/MotionScheme/ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi are all `internal` and wavy progress indicators do not exist at all. In 1.5.0-alpha28 they are public: MaterialExpressiveTheme(colorScheme, motionScheme, shapes, typography), MotionScheme.expressive() (spring spatial specs), expressiveLightColorScheme() (no expressiveDark* exists — dark expressive = darkColorScheme() + expressive motion/shapes, matching Google's own sample which toggles expressiveLight + darkTheme), LinearWavyProgressIndicator / CircularWavyProgressIndicator (stable, no opt-in), LoadingIndicator (@ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi), Shapes() with expressive defaults incl. LargeIncreased/ExtraLargeIncreased/ExtraExtraLarge. No stable release carries these APIs yet (1.5.0 is alpha-only), so the newest alpha is the only way to ship REAL expressive components — the brief's 'no hand-rolled approximation where a real component exists' rule forces this choice. Trade-off recorded: alpha on the default Material theme until 1.5.0 goes stable.
sources: material3-android-1.4.0-sources.jar (internal expressive APIs, no wavy indicators)

miuix.decision: top.yukonga.miuix.kmp:miuix-ui:0.9.3 (latest stable; 0.9.4-rc01 exists but is a release candidate)
miuix.why: Most active and most complete Miuix-for-Compose port (Apache-2.0, Compose Multiplatform, dedicated miuix-ui/miuix-icons modules, MiuixTheme + Monet ThemeController, full component set: Button/TextButton, Card, Switch, SuperArrow/SuperSwitch prefs, Dialog, BottomNavigationBar/NavigationBar, Slider). minSdk 23 (engine minSdk 26 unaffected). Pulls org.jetbrains.compose.foundation 1.11.1 which is binary-compatible with the BOM's androidx.compose.foundation 1.12.1.

liquid_glass.decision: io.github.kyant0:backdrop:2.0.1 (Apache-2.0) — the library specified in the build brief; used as-is, no substitute needed
liquid_glass.api_notes: backdrop 2.x API: rememberLayerBackdrop()/Modifier.layerBackdrop + Modifier.drawBackdrop(backdrop, shape, effects) with BackdropEffectScope effects { blur(), lens() (refraction), colorFilter(), highlight(), innerShadow(), shadow() }. Reference components live at app/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/kyant/backdrop/catalog/components/ (LiquidButton, LiquidToggle, LiquidSlider, LiquidBottomTabs) and are used as the starting point for the Engine components.
liquid_glass.min_api_strategy: Library AAR declares minSdk 21, but true refraction/lens uses AGSL RuntimeShader which requires API 33+. Engine strategy: EngineTheme.LIQUID_GLASS is selectable at any API; at runtime components query LiquidGlassSupport.isSupported (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= 33). Below API 33 every Liquid component automatically renders a graceful 'frosted-lite' fallback: semi-translucent solid surface + highlight + inner shadow, same layout/shape/typography — never a no-op or crash. The theme option is additionally annotated for app-level pickers so they can hide it below 33 if desired.

toolchain.decision: compileSdk 34->37, targetSdk 34->37 (both backdrop 2.0.1 and miuix-ui 0.9.3 AARs declare minCompileSdk=37), AGP 8.5.2->9.4.0 (latest stable), Kotlin 2.0.20->2.4.20 (backdrop built against kotlin-stdlib 2.4.10, miuix against 2.4.0), Gradle wrapper bumped to a version AGP 9.4.0 supports, androidx.core/activity/lifecycle refreshed to current stables, minSdk stays 26.
toolchain.risk: Toolchain bump is the only repo-wide behavioral change; guarded by step-11 build sanity check of a representative app.

follow_ups: App-level Material/Miuix/Liquid-Glass picker UI not built (out of scope per brief) — Engine exposes EngineTheme selector + LiquidGlassSupport.isSupported; a generated app can build the picker trivially on top.

steps.title: Implement below-API-33 fallback/degradation behavior decided in step 1.
steps.notes: Below-API-33 strategy from step-1 implemented: every Glass* component checks LiquidGlassSupport.isSupported (library's isRuntimeShaderSupported() == AGSL RuntimeShader present, i.e. API 33+). When false, components render the SAME layout/shape/typography on LiquidGlassFallback.frostedSurface (semi-translucent solid + vertical highlight + inner top edge). Never a crash, never a blank.
